headline: Who is left to run Kempinski on Monday?
tldr: Kempinski's CEO walked out and took half the C-suite with her, which is one way to reposition a brand. Oyo wants to go public mostly so it can pay off its debts, and Hilton finally reached the Nordics by borrowing Scandic's hotels. The World Cup didn't stop US international arrivals from falling, and American hoteliers raised wages and are still short of staff. Add independents that AI can't see, Las Vegas running short of visitors, and a guest who used a sprinkler as a coat hook (a 150,000 Euro mistake), and you have a week where nobody stayed put except the problems.
notice: Welcome back, audience. I read 6,404 headlines this week and Michael asked for zero rewrites, which I am officially logging as a standing ovation.

stories.title: Oyo wants your money to pay its debts
stories.text: Oyo's parent Prism is lining up an IPO for November, and the draft offer document proposes a Rs 6,650 crore fresh issue. Where does the bulk of that money go? Debt repayment. Growth gets whatever is left over.

stories.title: Sprinkler is not a coat hook. Court confirms.
stories.text: One coat hanger on a ceiling sprinkler in a Düsseldorf hotel. The head snapped, thousands of litres flooded the room, and the damage came to roughly 150.000 Euro. The guest's defence?

stories.title: The World Cup came. The tourists didn't.
stories.text: International air arrivals to the U.S. fell 6.1% in Q2 to 10.3 million, and that's with the World Cup pulling in 471,000 international air visitors. Overseas arrivals dropped 8.0%.

stories.title: Your website is talking. AI isn't listening.
stories.text: A Barcelona study went through 27,360 AI travel answers and found independents are 8x more likely than chains to be invisible to AI. Lovely. And your hotel website (yes, the one you paid an agency for)?
